items.label: f03-unescaped-ids
items.front: Row buttons interpolate ids raw into attributes (`data-edit-expense="${expense.id}"`, app.js:570-571, 615), and loadState (app.js:176-180) trusts whatever JSON is in localStorage.
items.back: A hand-edited or imported document can inject markup through an id attribute. App-minted UUIDs are safe, stored data is not. Fix: pass ids through the existing escapeHtml (app.js:765) like every other interpolated field.

items.label: f01-unguarded-writers
items.front: Reset, Delete and the bill-paid toggle each do `mutate state; saveState(); render();` (app.js:150-151, 584-585, 633-635). Storage is full, so setItem throws. What goes wrong?
items.back: State changes but storage does not, and render() is skipped because the exception escapes the listener: memory, storage and screen disagree, and a reload silently undoes the change. Fix: build a full replacement `next`, write it first, publish only on success (a shared commitState(next) helper), and tell the user on failure.

items.label: f04-two-tabs
items.front: Two tabs are open. Each keeps its own in-memory `state` and saves by writing the whole document (saveState, app.js:186-188); nothing listens for the `storage` event.
items.back: Last save wins: one tab silently overwrites the other tab's edits. Fix: listen for `storage` events and reload or merge before writing, or persist per record instead of the whole document.

items.label: f02-category-unvalidated
items.front: validateEntry (app.js:786-797) checks amount, decimals, description and date, but not category. Setting `#entryCategory` to a value outside the generated options (e.g. 'Travel') reads back as ''.
items.back: The expense is saved with category '' and its spending disappears from every budget bar. Fix: validate the category against the options updateCategoryOptions produced, not merely that it is non-empty.

items.label: f05-toggle-revert
items.front: You refactor the bill-paid toggle (app.js:631-637) to clone state, set `paid`, and call commitState(next); on failure it returns before render().
items.back: The checkbox still shows the new checked state, so the screen disagrees with state and storage. Fix: revert the control itself (`input.checked = !input.checked`) before returning, because no render() will correct the DOM.
